newsitem.title: GERMANY: German futures steady with range trade seen.
newsitem.headline: German futures steady with range trade seen.

text.p: German Bund futures were little changed from opening levels in late trade after dealers erased early gains with profit-taking.
Analysts said with the German interest rate picture set for the immediate future, the September future contract is likely to trade between 97.00 and 98.00.
The September DTB Bund future was down four basis points in late trade at 97.25, just off its low of the day at 97.22.
"The focus has moved to the U.S. again. Current ranges look pretty comfortable ," said Stuart Trow, analyst at Norinchukin International Plc.
Analysts said with the mark firm against European currencies, the short-end of the curve looks the strongest.
"Some further steepening of the yield curve looks like it may be the order of the day," one trader said.
Traders said with few big U.S. events scheduled, Bunds should hold the same spread to T-notes as today. The Bund/T-note spread slipped two basis points to minus 50 basis points in late trade.
Bunds were little affected by news from the German Finance Ministry that Germany will not be able to hold to its planned budget deficit of 60 billion marks in 1996.
Traders said despite government claims that the target could be met, the market had seen little chance for the deficit goal to be achieved.
Some said they see support for the contract around the 97.30 -- the closing level on Tuesday.
Resistance, on the other hand looms at around 97.70, a previous low for the contract when it was attempting a break above 98.00.
